newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Zsolnay porcelain factory to raise capital.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Zsolnay porcelain factory to raise capital.

text.p: The majority owner of Hungarian porcelain maker Zsolnay Rt will raise Zsolnay's share capital by 136 million forints from 700 million to finance technology development, APV said on Thursday.
"Via (the EU's) Phare-Hyferp program Zsolnay will receive a 0.7 million Ecu capital increase from MBFB," APV spokesman Adam Dudits told APV's weekly news conference.

Zsolnay will issue new liquidation preference shares, to be fully subscribed by the major shareholder state-owned investment and development bank Magyar Befektetesi es Fejlesztesi Bank (MBFB), he said.
Owners of the liqudition preference shares enjoy an absolute preference ahead other shareholders in case of liquidation of a company, Dudits said.
The 0.7 million Ecu is part of an 1.07 million Ecu financial assistance, of which the rest is to be spent on introducing western-style management and work culture in the company.
The share issue is expected to be approved at Zsolnay's extraordinary shareholders' meeting today.

Phare is the EU's technical aid programme set up to help eastern European countries in transition to market economy. Between 1990 and 1996 Phare has provided 81 million ECUs to support Hungary's privatisation process.
